svg.title: setup() runs in this order; control authority is released last
svg.text: setup() is non-virtual and runs in this order. The last two steps are the point of the ordering.
route assert failures to the log
seed every variable with its declared default
monitor writer, shell, logs, home-page tail; TX-drop watches
let the shell reach the live logger and alarm model
every task's one-time init: announce(), POST, the parameter load
the field is ours from here, and not before
tasks.setup() sits where it does because every log sink - the site's own included - must already exist for a
component's announce() or the POST verdict to land anywhere, and because the parameter load beside it is
hundreds of storage reads, which inside the first beat would read as a boot overrun against a 10 ms budget.
Control authority starts held, so nothing part-way through bring-up can energise an actuator on the way past.
